package_info.why_malicious: The package leverages obscure configuration options in .yarnrc or .npmrc to execute a hidden, attacker-controlled binary during package manager operations (e.g., yarn install), enabling arbitrary code execution without user awareness. The malicious binary is further obfuscated by using invisible Unicode characters in its filename, making detection by casual inspection difficult.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At package manager invocation, the configuration instructs yarn to execute a local binary (evil.sh) instead of the default yarn binary, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Redirecting the package manager to execute a local, potentially malicious binary is a classic method for achieving code execution on a victim's machine.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, .yarnrc or .npmrc files are used for benign configuration, not to redirect core binaries to attacker-controlled scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Advanced users may use yarnPath to point to a custom yarn binary for development or testing, but this is rare and should be explicit.
key_indicators: yarnPath/script-shell/git/shell fields pointing to local, non-standard binaries
Configuration files present in the project root with suspicious values

execution_context.file_location: project root directory (hidden file with invisible Unicode character in filename, e.g., evil<0x3164>.sh)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When invoked by the package manager due to the configuration, this hidden shell script executes arbitrary attacker-supplied commands, potentially compromising the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A hidden executable file with a non-printable or invisible Unicode character in its name is highly unusual and designed to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not include hidden executables with obfuscated names intended to be run by the package manager.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason to hide executables with invisible Unicode characters in open source packages.
key_indicators: Executable files with invisible or non-printable Unicode characters in their names
Presence of shell scripts not referenced in package.json but invoked via configuration

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates a package with a hidden malicious binary (using invisible Unicode characters in the filename).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binary is present in the project root, but not easily visible to users.

attack_chain.action: Attacker adds a .yarnrc (or .npmrc) file that configures the package manager to use the hidden binary as its main executable.
attack_chain.leads_to: Package manager is now configured to execute the attacker's binary on install.

attack_chain.action: Victim runs yarn install (or equivalent), triggering execution of the hidden malicious binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on the victim's machine (e.g., reverse shell, data exfiltration, etc.)

behavioral_signatures: Project-level .yarnrc or .npmrc files specifying yarnPath, script-shell, or similar fields pointing to local binaries
Execution of non-standard binaries during package manager operations
Presence of hidden or oddly named executable files in the project root
file_indicators: .yarnrc or .npmrc with yarnPath/script-shell/git/shell fields referencing local files
Executable files in the project root with invisible or non-printable Unicode characters in their names
network_indicators: Any unexpected outbound network connections initiated during package installation (depends on payload in malicious binary)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for .yarnrc or .npmrc files in project roots that set yarnPath, script-shell, git, or shell to local files. Flag any referenced binaries that are not standard package manager binaries, especially those with invisible or non-printable Unicode characters in their names. Monitor for execution of unexpected binaries during package manager operations. Use file system tools to reveal hidden files and check for suspicious executables. Alert on any outbound network activity during package installation that is not typical for the package.
